newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 31.

text.p: Mexico's crude shipping ports closed because of winds were all reopened Friday as climate conditions improved, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its 1000 local/1600 GMT daily report.
Crude shipping ports Pajaritos in Veracruz state and Dos Bocas in Tabasco state reopened Thursday after being closed for three consecutive days.
Salina Cruz in Oaxaca, Coatzacoalcos in Veracruz and Dos Bocas remained shut for smaller tourist and fishing ships.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.
Possible showers along coasts of Sonora, Sinaloa, Nayarit, Colima and Michoacan states.

Relaxed winds except for in the Gulf of Tehuantepec, where winds for the northeast were registered from 20 to 25 knots (38 to 47 km/22 to 28 miles per hour) and waves to nine and 11 feet high. -- Gulf of Mexico:

Mass of cold air continues to lower temperatures with probable rains along coasts of Veracruz, Tamaulipas, Tabasco and Campeche. Winds from northeast at 10 to 15 knots (19 to 29 km/11 to 17 miles per hour) and waves four to six feet high. -- Caribbean:

Isolated light rains along coast of Quintana Roo state and along Central America. Winds from the northeast at 10 to 20 knots (19 to 38 km/11 to 22 miles per hour) and waves four to six feet high expected to relax later in the day.
